A.note: Strongest is its principled refusal to compute per-member shares or a concentration index over a member set containing negatives; weakest is that it re-averages already-averaged values across a hopping window and presents thirteen output columns as five metrics.

B.note: Strongest is converting the half-hourly means to MWh with the declared period length so the window sums are volumes rather than means of means; weakest is that those six-hour sums silently assume twelve periods are present while the completeness counter is explicitly left out.

C.note: Strongest is the explicit refusal to treat any mean as an instantaneous value or to synthesise a period end, with a spacing guard that nulls rather than fabricates a ramp; weakest is the LEFT JOIN between a per-event step and a windowed step, whose acceptance it cannot vouch for.

D.note: Strongest is grounding every sum and every omission in the declared statistic, unit, supportPeriod and phenomenonTimeRelation rather than in fuel-name intuition; weakest is that refusing all cross-record aggregation leaves the selection thin, with a data-quality flag occupying one of the five slots.

blinding.why: D quotes named annotations — semanticRole, observedProperty, unit, statistic, phenomenonTimeRelation, supportPeriod and dcterms:identifier — and specification text that A states outright are absent from its material, so D appears to have had the most to work with.
